rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person unable to find an offering must fast three days during the Hajj months, preferably on Dhu al-Hijja 7–9, and seven after returning.
rows.anchor: üç gün hacda, yedi de döndüğünüzde oruç tutması lâzımdır. Hacdaki hac ayları içinde tutulur ki müstehabı zilhiccenin yedinci, sekizinci, dokuzuncu günleridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven fasts after return are kept after completing the Hajj rites; al-Shafiʿi says they should be after rejoining one's family.
rows.anchor: Dönüşteki de ef‘âl-i hacdan fâriğ olunca ve Şâfiî’ye göre ehl ü ‘iyâline kavuştuğunda tutulmalıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The substitute fasts total ten; the text should not be understood to allow either the three or the seven alone.
rows.anchor: Sakın terdid veya tahyir suretiyle üç veya yedi kifayet eder zannedilmesin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose households are not among the residents of the Sacred Mosque are people from beyond the miqat, since miqat residents and those nearer can enter Mecca without ihram.
rows.anchor: ehl ü ‘iyâli Mescid-i Harâm huzzârından olmayan kimseler içindir. Ki bunlar meskenleri mîkāt hâricinde olan âfâkīlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi interprets the people present at the Sacred Mosque as those traveling from a distance that permits shortened prayer in Mecca.
rows.anchor: İmam Şâfiî bunları Mekke’de kasr-ı salât edecek kadar bir mesâfe-i seferden gelenler

rows.speaker: Tâvûs
rows.claim: Tawus interprets them as people of the outer sanctuary, beyond the Meccan Haram.
rows.anchor: Tâvûs “Harem-i Mekke mâverâsından olan ehl-i hil”

rows.speaker: İmam Mâlik
rows.claim: Malik interprets them simply as everyone other than the inhabitants of Mecca.
rows.anchor: İmam Mâlik de “Bizzat Mekke ahâlisinin gayrı” diye anlamışlardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qiran and tamattu apply to non-local people beyond the miqat who cannot enter Mecca without ihram; those of the sanctuary and its environs should perform ifrad.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı hacc-ı kıran ve temettu‘mâverâ-yı mîkāt ahâlisinden bulunan ve Mekke’ye ihramsız girmeleri câiz olmayan âfâkīler hakkındadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage closes by telling pilgrims to complete Hajj and ʿumra for God, avoid disobedience especially in Hajj, and remember God's severe punishment.
rows.anchor: ve Allah’a isyandan sakınınız ve bâhusûs emr-i hacda pek ittikālı olunuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUrza denotes something stretched as a restraint or barrier, or something continually exposed like a target.
rows.anchor: “‘Urza”: Gergi ve mâni‘a yahut açıktan hedef gibi bir şeye mâruz olup duran demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yamin means strength or firmness and, by extension, an oath that invokes God's name to reinforce a promise made before God; false swearing is a grave sin.
rows.anchor: Esasen kuvvet ve sağlamlık demektir. Bu münasebetle sağ ele “yemîn” denildiği gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Īlā is an oath not to have intercourse with one's wife.
rows.anchor: Şer‘an zevcesine mücâma‘at etmemek üzere yemin etmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talāq is the legal removal of the marriage bond; its lexical sense is to release or loosen a bond.
rows.anchor: Şer‘an kayd-ı nikâhın ref‘idir ki lisânımızda “boşamak” denilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿrūf first means what is recognized, then denotes every act judged good by reason or religious law; it contrasts with munkar and includes justice, fairness, generosity, and good treatment.
rows.anchor: akıl veya şer‘ile hüsnü tanınan her fiile isim” olmuş bir kelime-i câmi‘adır ki mukabili “münker”dir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns against using God as a pretext or obstacle through oaths that prevent keeping one's word, piety, or reconciliation; avoid such oaths and do not treat keeping them as pleasing God.
rows.anchor: Allah’ı yeminlerinize mâruz kılıp durmayınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording may mean not swearing often so one can be good, pious, and a peacemaker; alternatively, do not swear even for those good purposes or use an oath to block them.
rows.anchor: Yani Allah’a çok yemin etmezseniz, bârr, müttakī, muslih olabilirsiniz veya birr ü takvâ ve dargınlıkları barıştırmak için de olsa Allah’a çok yemin etmeyiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic hadith instructs someone who swears an oath and then sees a better course to do the better thing and expiate the oath.
rows.anchor: bir kimse bir şeye yemin eder de sonra gayrısını daha hayırlı görürse o hayırlı şeyi yapsın ve yemînine keffâret versin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported occasion is that Abdullah b. Rawaha swore not to visit or speak with his brother-in-law Bashir b. Nuʿman, nor reconcile him with his sister, then claimed he could not break his oath.
rows.anchor: Rivayet olunduğuna göre Abdullah b. Revâha bir kırgınlık hasebiyle eniştesi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is also reported to have been revealed over an oath by Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: Bu âyet bunun veya Hazret-i Ebû Bekir’in bir yemini hakkında nâzil olmuştur

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Âişe
rows.claim: Aisha says the verse was revealed against repeating oaths to God.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Âişe demiştir ki bu âyet Allah’a yemini tekrar etmek aleyhinde nâzil olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears the oaths people make and knows their intentions.
rows.anchor: Allah Semî‘dir, yapılan yemînleri işitir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laghw is speech that has no legal weight; a vain oath is made without a binding intention, such as swearing on one's honest but mistaken belief about a fact.
rows.anchor: “Lağv”; derece-i i‘tibardan sâkıt olan kelâm demektir, yemîn-i lağv da bir akd ü kasıt bulunmayan yemindir

rows.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
rows.claim: Al-Shafiʿi defines a vain oath as habitual emphatic phrases like “no, by God” or “yes, by God,” said without intending an oath, and holds that no expiation is due.
rows.anchor: İmam Şâfiî yemîn-i lağvı lisanda “hayır vallahi, evet vallahi” gibi mücerred tekid için söylenip half mânası hatıra gelmeyen elfâz-ı yemîne haml etmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accountability denied here is in the afterlife, not the worldly expiation discussed in Sura al-Anʿam; thus a mistaken, non-deceptive oath is not punished.
rows.anchor: Lâkin bu âyetteki muâhazeden murâd, muâhaze-i uhreviye olup muâhaze-i dünyeviye olan keffâret demek olmadığı zâhirdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By contrast, a deliberate false oath is a yamin ghamus: it is sinful, and expiation cannot release the person from its sin.
rows.anchor: yalan kasdıyla, bile bile yalan olarak yapılan yeminlerle muâhaze eder. Buna “yemîn-i gamûs” denilir ki keffâreti yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God overlooks vain oaths because of His abundant forgiveness and forbearance, not because they are inherently sinful.
rows.anchor: lağv yeminlerle haddizâtında günah olmadıkları için değil, gufrân ü hilminin çokluğundan dolayı muâhaze etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A binding oath (yamin munʿaqida) is a conditional commitment to do or not do something in the future.
rows.anchor: istikbalde bir şey yapmaya veya yapmamaya azmedilir ve bu suretle ta‘lîkī bir akid yapılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command concerns usury still unpaid and uncollected; the previously received amounts remain as covered by the rule that what is past belongs to the recipient.
rows.anchor: فَلَهُۥ مَا سَلَفَ hükmünce geçmiş olan ribânın makbûza mahsus olduğundan gaflet etmeyiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Genuine, complete faith entails acting by leaving the remaining usury.
rows.anchor: Zira îmân-ı kâmil ameli istilzâm eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who refuse to stop either disbelieve the prohibition or believe it but persist in practice; the verse warns them of war from God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: Şayet yapmazsanız, yani Allah’tan korkmaz da ribânın haram olduğuna inanmaz veya inanır da terk etmezseniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: According to the alternative reading fa-adhinū, the command means that the offenders themselves should declare war on God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: Yahut -فَأْذَنُوا۟ kıraatine göre- Allah ve Resûlü tarafından kendinize harb ilan ediniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who persist are either apostates who deem usury lawful or sinful believers who knowingly disobey; both face the war command, like zakat deniers or refusers, who are apostates or rebels.
rows.anchor: gerek ribâ helâldir itikadına avdet etmiş mürted veya nakz-ı ‘ahd etmiş kâfir olsun, gerekse hurmetine iman eder ve fakat imanıyla amel etmez mü’min-i fâsık olsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoiding usury is an individual duty for Muslims, while abolishing usurious dealings throughout society is a major collective duty because widespread practice makes individual avoidance difficult or perhaps impossible.
rows.anchor: ribâdan sakınmak tâbi‘iyyet-i İslâmiyede bulunanların hepsine farz-ı ‘ayn bir vazîfe-i ferdiye olduktan başka sûret-i umûmiyede ribâ muâmelesini kaldırmak da mühim bir farîza-i ictimâ‘iyedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hanafi school explicitly holds that the prohibition of usury between Muslims and non-Muslims falls away in a non-Muslim territory; the author suggests this may explain why the ban was not announced until Muslims gained military capacity.
rows.anchor: dâr-i küfürde bulunan bir Müslümandan müslim ile gayr-i müslim beyninde ribânın hurmeti sâkıt olacağı mezheb-i Hanefî’de musarrahtır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An Islamic government disciplines individual usurers; if they resist the government individually or collectively, declaring war becomes the religious duty of all Muslims.
rows.anchor: Bunlar ferd veya cemaat hâlinde hükûmete karşı korlarsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the present condition, Muslims have lost collective capacity to enforce this duty, so abstaining from usury remains largely individual and its social prevalence makes that difficult.
rows.anchor: bu vazifelerini unutmuş ve bunun tatbîki husûsunda ictimâ‘î istitâ‘atlarını zâyi‘etmiş bir hâl-i tezebzübde bulunduklarından bi’l-amel ribâdan kaçınmak sırf ferdî bir vazife gibi kalmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: War from God and His Messenger can describe literal warfare or figuratively warn of the crime's magnitude; either way, usury's consumer and provider cannot escape divine material and spiritual conflict.
rows.anchor: “Allah ve Resûlünün harbi” tâbiri bazen hakikaten harbde bazen de cürmün azametini ve zararını tasvir için makām-ı inzarda mecaz olarak kullanılır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic hadith says, or invokes a curse, against the person who consumes usury and the one who provides it.
rows.anchor: bir hadîs-i nebevîde “لَعَنَ اللّٰهُّٰ آكِلَ الرِّبَا وَمُوكِلَهُ: Allah ribâ yiyeni ve yedireni lanetledi”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On repentance, creditors may recover their principal without taking more or being forced to accept less; refusal to repent exposes them to losses through their apostasy or injustice.
rows.anchor: re’sü’l-mâllarınız sizindir. Onları alırsınız, o suretle ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage addresses Muslims who had converted while still holding unpaid claims from their former usury transactions.
rows.anchor: mukaddemâ yaptıkları ribâ mu‘âmelâtından henüz kabz etmedikleri alacakları kalmış olan birtakım kimseler hakkında nâzil olduğu anlaşılıyor

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: Muqatil says the verses concerned four Thaqif brothers, Masʿud, Abd Yalil, Habib, and Rabiʿa of Banu Amr b. Umayr, who lent to Banu Mughira in Mecca and sought interest after converting.
rows.anchor: Mukātil’in rivayetine göre Tâif’te Sakif kabilesinden Benû Amr b. Umeyr denilen Mes‘ud

rows.speaker: Mukātil
rows.claim: In Muqatil's account, Banu Mughira refused the interest, the dispute went to governor Attab b. Asid, and the Prophet instructed him to offer terms and declare war if they refused.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’a yazdı, o zaman bu âyet nâzil oldu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the Taif peace settlement with the Prophet stipulated that Saqif's usury receivables and payables were abandoned.
rows.anchor: bir rivayete göre Sakif’in Hazret-i Peygamber ile Tâif musâlahasında halk üzerinde ribâdan olan gerek alacak ve gerek vereceklerinin mevzû‘

rows.speaker: Atâ ve İkrime
rows.claim: Ata and Ikrima say Abbas and Uthman had made a prepaid date purchase, collected part of the dates, then added interest to the remainder before the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: Atâ ve İkrime’nin beyanlarına göre ‘amm-i Nebî Hazret-i Abbas b. Abdülmuttalib ile dâmâd-ı Nebî Hazret-i Osman b. Affan

rows.speaker: Süddî
rows.claim: Suddi reports that Abbas and Khalid b. Walid had partnered in interest-bearing credit dealings before Islam and still had many such claims when they converted.
rows.anchor: Süddî’nin rivayetine göre Hazret-i Abbas ile Hazret-i Hâlid b. Velîd câhiliyede şerîk olarak ribâ ile veresiye muâmele yapıyorlardı

rows.speaker: İbn Ömer ve Câbir
rows.claim: In reports graded authentic by the author, Ibn Umar and Jabir say the Prophet declared in the Farewell Hajj sermon that all pre-Islamic usury was void and Abbas's was the first he abolished.
rows.anchor: sahîha ile tahrîc olunduğuna göre; İbn Ömer’le Câbir radıyallâhu ‘anhümâ bizzat Hazret-i Peygamber’den şöyle rivayet etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chronology places the verse before the conquest of Mecca; the Farewell sermon later implemented its general rule by retaining what had been received and voiding what remained unpaid, with Abbas's claims as the first application rather than necessarily its specific occasion.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Abbas’ın fâizleri âyetin bilhassa sebeb-i nüzûlü değilse bile, umûmî olan hükmünün Mekke’de ilk mevrid-i tatbîki olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For converts, pre-Islamic transactions valid among them are not annulled from their beginning; consequences after conversion are settled under Islamic law.
rows.anchor: Bunların zamân-ı küfürlerinde ahkâm-ı İslâm’a muhalif ve fakat beynlerinde muteber olmak üzere yaptıkları sâbık muâmeleler, esasından fesh u nakz edilmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prior marriage valid before conversion but prohibited in Islam is recognized for the past, including its unpaid dower, but cannot continue; the spouses are separated and a proper dower is owed if none was paid.
rows.anchor: bu nikâh sâbıka nazaran muteberdir. Verilen mehir geri alınmaz. Fakat ba‘de’l-İslâm ibkā da edilmez, beynleri tefrik olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By implication, the rule extends beyond usury: contracts made in a territory of war are not retrospectively annulled after conquest, received payments are not returned, and invalid terms cannot be continued.
rows.anchor: Bu beyânâttan şu neticeleri alabiliriz: Evvelâ, âyet-i ribânın nüzûlü sade Haccetü’l-vedâ‘dan değil feth-i Mekke’den bile biraz mukaddem imiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The war command for usury applies within Islamic territory to apostates or sinful Muslims; Muslims need not wage war on foreign lands to abolish usury, but must protect their own society from it.
rows.anchor: Sâniyen ribâ için kâfir veya âsîye i‘lân-ı harb farîzası dâr-ı harbde değil, dâr-ı İslâm içinde ve tâbi‘iyyet-i İslâmiyeyi kabul etmiş olanlara nazaran bir hükümdür

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet required treaty-bound Christians of Najran to avoid usury and disassociate from those who practiced it, warning them of war; a protected community's covenant equates legally to Muslim faith in transactions, though not worship.
rows.anchor: zimmet-i İslâm’a giren Necran Nasârâsına ribâ yememek ve ribâ yiyenden zimmeti berî olmak üzere ahid vermiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Islamic territory, usury practitioners merit God's and the Messenger's war whether they act from apostasy or sinful disobedience; repentant debtors retain principal, subject to their ability to pay.
rows.anchor: her iki surette de Allah’ın ve Resûlünün harbine müstahiktir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An insolvent debtor must be given time until able to pay; forgiving the debt is better and brings greater reward than waiting.
rows.anchor: o hâlde hüküm bi’z-zarûre hâl-i yüsrüne intizardır. Ona verebilecek bir hâle gelinceye kadar mühlet verilmek lâzım gelir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule extends by implication to all debts: an insolvent debtor should not be imprisoned, and helping poor debtors escape debt through aid or remission is a major good.
rows.anchor: Bu âyetin hükmü bi’d-delâle bütün düyûnâta şâmildir. Bu da ahkâm-ı müdâyenâtta bir esastır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Resurrection, every person receives the full result of their deeds; even those exposed to lasting punishment are not wronged because they receive what they earned.
rows.anchor: Bu kıyamette müebbeden azab ve ukūbete de mâruz olsalar bunda mazlum bulunmayacaklar, çünkü kendi kazançlarını alacaklardır

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports this as the Quran's last-revealed verse, following 4:176 and 5:3 during the Prophet's Farewell Hajj; Gabriel ordered it placed at the start of 2:280, and the Prophet lived 81 days, with other reports giving 21, seven, or three hours.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretlerinden mervîdir ki bu âyet Kur’ân’ın en son nâzil olan âyetidir. Şöyle ki Resûlullah haccettiği zaman âyet-i kelâle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is fitting that the last-revealed verse warns of death and Resurrection; its placement after usury and among debt rules is eloquent and meaningful.
rows.anchor: son nâzil olan bu âyetin vefâtı ve yevm-i kıyâmeti ihtar ederek nâzil olması pek mânidar olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage moves from charity to buying and usury as means of earning, then to debt; because debt rests on promise and human responsibility, God ties it to piety and next explains written documentation and other debt rules.
rows.anchor: Ahkâm-ı infâk, vesâit-i kesbden olan bey‘ü ribâ ahkâmına, bu da ahkâm-ı müdâyenâta müncer olmuş
